summary: NASA's GRACE satellites show about 32 km³ of water lost under the Qassim region of Saudi Arabia since 2003, and the loss has sped up since 2018. Farms pump most of it. From 16 November 2026, year-round fodder is banned there, so many center-pivot farmers must pick a new crop now. Qatra shows each farmer the groundwater cost of every option on their own field. The farmer clicks their pivot on a Sentinel-2 map. Qatra reads what it really grew from 11 years of Landsat, estimates what it pumps with NASA POWER weather and the FAO-56 method, and ranks five crop options by the farmer's own priorities, starting from what the field grows now. Our water estimate is within 1% of a flux-tower measurement on a Saudi alfalfa pivot, so we give results within about ±15%. Example: Field 1, a 33-hectare fodder pivot, pumped about 950,000 m³ in 2024-25. Switching to berseem clover, a winter fodder that is still allowed, would save about 670,000 m³ a year. We ran the same method on 1,553 pivots across central Qassim: moving its 93 year-round pivots to berseem would save about 43 million m³ a year.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

From 16 November 2026, MEWA stops year-round (perennial) fodder in Qassim and the other sedimentary-shelf regions, so every pivot that grows alfalfa or Rhodes grass all year must pick a new crop. Qatra answers one question for one farmer: what should this field grow next, and what will each option cost in groundwater and earn? Live demo: https://mbassam2009.github.io/qatra/

HOW IT WORKS

1. NASA GRACE/GRACE-FO shows the regional problem: about 32 km³ of water lost under the Qassim area since 2003, faster since 2018.

2. Fields: 14 real pivots near Unaizah, found on a Sentinel-2 image and shown every month from space.

3. Landsat 8/9 (299 scenes, 2015-2025) gives each field's greenness and shows what it really grew. Field 1 was bare 2017-2019 and green all year since 2020.

4. NASA POWER daily weather gives reference ET with the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith method: 2,547 mm a year against 80 mm of rain. Pumped water = crop coefficient × reference ET, minus useful rain, divided by 80% pivot efficiency.

5. Five options are compared: year-round fodder (banned after 16 Nov), berseem clover then bare summer, wheat then bare summer, faba bean then bare summer, and wheat and faba bean in turns. For each: water per hectare and for the whole field, change from today, heat-stress days, a soil score, crop value and value per m³ of water.

6. Six sliders (save water, build soil, avoid heat, earn more, sure buyer, least change) rank the options, starting from what the field grows now.

7. Ground check: our water estimate is within 1% of an eddy-covariance flux tower on a Saudi alfalfa pivot (2,406 vs 2,430 mm a year), so results carry about ±15%. ECOSTRESS is used to track crop state.

8. Scaling: the same method found 1,553 pivots on a 73 × 69 km area of central Qassim. Any pivot can be clicked to see 12 monthly Sentinel-2 images and its options.

RESULTS AND BENEFITS

Field 1 (33 ha) pumped about 950,000 m³ in 2024-25. Berseem, a winter fodder that is still allowed, would save about 670,000 m³ a year; faba bean about 830,000. The 93 year-round pivots on our map pump about 65 million m³ a year; moving them to berseem would save about 43 million m³. Farmers see the water cost of a crop before they plant, for their own field, in numbers they can act on.

INTENDED IMPACT

Help farmers pick a legal, profitable replacement for fodder that uses far less groundwater, and give MEWA a field-by-field picture of where the water goes. Next: MEWA well-meter data (Hafiz) to check our numbers, a comparison with KAUST's study of 35,000 pivots, an Arabic phone app tested with farmers, and scaling to all of Saudi Arabia.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Most satellite studies measure the water fields already used. Qatra looks forward: what to plant next on this field, and what it will cost. It starts from what the satellite shows the field grows now, so it does not tell every farm to grow beans, and every option shows its evidence and limits so the farmer stays the one who decides.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

The new fodder rule; what farmers already know how to grow and sell (berseem keeps the same buyers and balers); demand (Saudi Arabia imports over 90% of the faba beans it eats); crop income; soil health; summer heat; and honest uncertainty. Pumping cost is not included yet.

TOOLS

Python (pandas, NumPy, OpenCV, netCDF4), the FAO-56 method, NASA POWER API, Microsoft Planetary Computer API (Landsat, Sentinel-2), NASA AppEEARS (ECOSTRESS), CSR GRACE mascons, a standalone HTML/SVG/JavaScript web app on GitHub Pages, and an optional Streamlit app. No hardware.
